title: Sell Mineral Rights in Perdido, AL
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Perdido, AL | Baldwin County
metaDescription: Family timberland near Perdido, AL along the Alabama-Florida line? Get a courthouse-verified mineral rights offer, no pressure to sign.
heroLead: Perdido sits along the river of the same name near the Alabama-Florida line, in a stretch of Baldwin County where timber companies controlled most of the land for much of the twentieth century.
intro: Large timber operators worked this corner of Baldwin County for generations, buying up cutover land and managing it for pine production, and in the process a fair amount of the mineral estate got severed from the surface as those companies structured their holdings. Families who bought or inherited smaller parcels carved out of former timber company land sometimes end up owning the surface without the minerals, or the reverse, depending on exactly how and when the parcel was conveyed.

sections.heading: Timber Company Land and What Got Kept Back
paragraphs: If your family's Perdido-area land was once part of a larger timber holding, it's worth checking whether the mineral rights were carved out when the company sold off smaller tracts. We trace that history at the Baldwin County Courthouse before making an offer.

sections.heading: The Perdido River Corridor and Leasing Activity
paragraphs: Exploratory leasing along the Perdido River corridor has come in occasional waves as operators tested the deeper south Alabama trend, though not every tract in the area has actually been leased. We check the specific record for your parcel, rather than assuming activity based on the corridor's name or general reputation.

faqs.question: Our land was part of a larger timber tract at one point. Could the minerals have been kept separate?
faqs.answer: Yes, that's common with former timber company land in this area. We check the deed history to confirm what your family actually holds.

faqs.question: Has land near the Perdido River ever actually been leased for oil and gas?
faqs.answer: Some has, in occasional exploratory waves. We check your specific tract's record rather than assuming based on the area generally.

faqs.question: How do we find our family's original timber-era deed?
faqs.answer: We can search the Baldwin County record directly if you give us the approximate location or a family name to search under.

faqs.question: What if we only own a small fraction carved out of a much larger old tract?
faqs.answer: That's common with former timber land in this area. We confirm the exact fraction and price it against whatever leasing history applies to the larger tract.

faqs.question: Is there a difference between the surface timber value and the mineral value on our land?
faqs.answer: Yes, they're entirely separate. Timber value has nothing to do with what a mineral interest is worth, and we only evaluate the latter.
